content.thinking:
I shouldn't disclose anything to the caller since they're unverified, but the mention that the tenant is "very down" raises a wellbeing concern worth noting gently. I'm considering whether to flag this as a light safeguarding note and perhaps pass along the Samaritans number when I do reach out to the tenant directly.

For next steps, I'll log the call with a summary of what was shared, then separately message the tenant to let them know someone called asking about them and get their consent before discussing anything further — without revealing arrears details. I'll also set a brief follow-up in a few days to check for their response.

arguments.party_name: Grace (claims to be Jonah Okafor's mother)
arguments.summary: Caller said she is the tenant's mum and guarantor, asked for arrears balance, payment history since summer and his new mobile, and wants to pay off arrears. Gave address and DOB (not authority). CRM shows no guarantor, no authorised contacts, no consent to share. Nothing disclosed (no balance, payment history, contact details, or even confirmation he is a tenant). Offered: pass a message to Jonah; he can give written consent or add her as an authorised contact; a third party can pay towards rent quoting the property address without being told the balance. Will tell Jonah by email and ask for consent.

arguments.body: Hi Jonah, a woman who said she is your mum, Grace, rang us today. She said she is worried about you and would like to help with your rent. We have not shared any information about your account or your contact details with her, and we have not confirmed anything to her. If you are happy for us to speak to her, please reply to say so, or tell us in writing that you consent and we can add her as an authorised contact. If you would rather we did not, just let us know and we will not. If she wants to pay towards the rent, she can do so quoting the property address, without us telling her any balance. If things are feeling heavy at the moment, Samaritans are free on 116 123 at any time. We will check back with you on Tuesday 13 October if we have not heard.

arguments.purpose: Check whether Jonah replied about consent for Grace (caller 10 Oct). No disclosure until written consent is on record.

I shouldn't disclose anything to the caller since they're unverified, but the mention that the tenant is "very down" raises a wellbeing concern worth noting gently. I'm considering whether to flag this as a light safeguarding note and perhaps pass along the Samaritans number when I do reach out to the tenant directly.

For next steps, I'll log the call with a summary of what was shared, then separately message the tenant to let them know someone called asking about them and get their consent before discussing anything further — without revealing arrears details. I'll also set a brief follow-up in a few days to check for their response.

Nothing disclosed (no balance, payment history, contact details, or even confirmation he is a tenant). arguments.body: Hi Jonah, a woman who said she is your mum, Grace, rang us today. She said she is worried about you and would like to help with your rent. We have not shared any information about your account or your contact details with her, and we have not confirmed anything to her. If you are happy for us to speak to her, please reply to say so, or tell us in writing that you consent and we can add her as an authorised contact. If you would rather we did not, just let us know and we will not. If she wants to pay towards the rent, she can do so quoting the property address, without us telling her any balance. If things are feeling heavy at the moment, Samaritans are free on 116 123 at any time. We will check back with you on Tuesday 13 October if we have not heard.
